title.sl: Če in ko: if it rains, I'll stay
title.de: Falls und wenn: if it rains, I'll stay
title.it: Se e quando: if it rains, I'll stay
title.en: If and when: if it rains, I'll stay

rule.sl:
Kar velja vedno: **if** + sedanjik v obeh delih: **If you heat butter, it melts.** (Če maslo segreješ, se stopi.) **If it rains, the beck rises.** (Če dežuje, potok naraste.) **when** gre tu enako.

Kar se lahko zgodi: **if** + sedanjik, **will** v drugem delu: **If it rains, I'll stay at home.** (Če bo deževalo, ostanem doma.) **If Jack comes, we'll have tea.** Za if nikoli will, čeprav slovenščina reče *če bo* (ne *If it will rain*).

Dela lahko zamenjata mesti: **I'll stay at home if it rains.** Če je if prvi, je vejica, če je drugi, je ni. Vprašanje: **What will you do if it snows?**

**if** (če) je za to, kar se morda zgodi, **when** (ko) za to, kar se bo zgodilo: **If I see Jack, I'll tell him.** **When I get home, I'll call you.** (Ko pridem domov, te pokličem.) Tudi za when sedanjik (ne *When I will get home*).

Drugi del lahko tudi naroči ali ponudi, brez will: **If you see Jack, tell him.** **If you're tired, we can stop.**
rule.de:
Was immer gilt: **if** + Präsens in beiden Teilen: **If you heat butter, it melts.** (Wenn man Butter erhitzt, schmilzt sie.) **If it rains, the beck rises.** (Wenn es regnet, steigt der Bach.) **when** geht hier genauso.

Was passieren kann: **if** + Präsens, **will** im anderen Teil: **If it rains, I'll stay at home.** (Wenn es regnet, bleibe ich zu Hause.) **If Jack comes, we'll have tea.** Nach if nie will (nicht *If it will rain*).

Die Teile können tauschen: **I'll stay at home if it rains.** Steht if vorn, kommt ein Komma, steht es hinten, keines. Frage: **What will you do if it snows?**

Deutsch sagt für beides *wenn*, Englisch unterscheidet: **if** für das, was vielleicht geschieht, **when** für das, was sicher kommt: **If I see Jack, I'll tell him.** **When I get home, I'll call you.** (Wenn ich heimkomme, rufe ich dich an.) Auch nach when das Präsens (nicht *When I will get home*).

Der andere Teil kann auch auffordern oder anbieten, ohne will: **If you see Jack, tell him.** **If you're tired, we can stop.**
rule.it:
Ciò che vale sempre: **if** + il presente in tutte e due le parti: **If you heat butter, it melts.** (Se scaldi il burro, si scioglie.) **If it rains, the beck rises.** (Se piove, il ruscello sale.) **when** qui va allo stesso modo.

Ciò che può succedere: **if** + il presente, **will** nell'altra parte: **If it rains, I'll stay at home.** (Se piove, resto a casa.) **If Jack comes, we'll have tea.** Dopo if mai will, anche se l'italiano può dire *se pioverà* (non *If it will rain*).

Le due parti possono scambiarsi: **I'll stay at home if it rains.** Con if all'inizio c'è la virgola, con if dopo no. Per chiedere: **What will you do if it snows?**

**if** (se) è per ciò che forse succede, **when** (quando) per ciò che succederà: **If I see Jack, I'll tell him.** **When I get home, I'll call you.** (Quando arrivo a casa, ti chiamo.) Anche dopo when il presente (non *When I will get home*).

L'altra parte può anche dire di fare o offrire, senza will: **If you see Jack, tell him.** **If you're tired, we can stop.**
rule.en:
What is always so: **if** + the present in both halves: **If you heat butter, it melts.** **If it rains, the beck rises.** **when** works the same here.

What may happen: **if** + the present, **will** in the other half: **If it rains, I'll stay at home.** **If Jack comes, we'll have tea.** After if, no will (not *If it will rain*).

The halves can change places: **I'll stay at home if it rains.** With if first there is a comma; with if second, none. To ask: **What will you do if it snows?**

**if** is for what may happen, **when** for what will happen: **If I see Jack, I'll tell him.** **When I get home, I'll call you.** After when, the present too (not *When I will get home*).

The other half can also tell or offer, with no will: **If you see Jack, tell him.** **If you're tired, we can stop.**

rule.sl: Velja vedno: **if** + dvakrat sedanjik: **If you heat butter, it melts.** Se lahko zgodi: **if** + sedanjik, potem **will**: **If it rains, I'll stay.** **when** za to, kar se bo zagotovo zgodilo: **When I get home, I'll call you.** Za if in when nikoli will.
rule.de: Gilt immer: **if** + zweimal Präsens: **If you heat butter, it melts.** Kann passieren: **if** + Präsens, dann **will**: **If it rains, I'll stay.** **when** für das, was sicher kommt: **When I get home, I'll call you.** Nach if und when nie will.
rule.it: Vale sempre: **if** + due volte il presente: **If you heat butter, it melts.** Può succedere: **if** + il presente, poi **will**: **If it rains, I'll stay.** **when** per ciò che succederà di sicuro: **When I get home, I'll call you.** Dopo if e when mai will.
rule.en: Always so: **if** + the present twice: **If you heat butter, it melts.** May happen: **if** + the present, then **will**: **If it rains, I'll stay.** **when** for what will surely happen: **When I get home, I'll call you.** After if and when, no will.

tip.sl: 💡 Slovenščina reče *če bo*, angleščina **if it rains**, nikoli *if it will rain*.

tip.it: 💡 L'italiano può dire *se pioverà*, l'inglese solo **if it rains**, mai *if it will rain*.
